title: PetitPotam / NTLM Relay (Authentication Coercion)
description: Authentication-coercion techniques (such as PetitPotam via MS-EFSRPC) force a Windows host, including a Domain Controller, to authenticate to an attacker-controlled machine using NTLM. The relayed authentication can then be forwarded to a service that does not enforce signing or channel binding, most notably Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) web enrollment, to obtain a certificate and impersonate the victim machine, leading to domain compromise.
businessImpact: Critical --- relaying a coerced Domain Controller authentication to AD CS can yield a certificate for the DC and result in full domain takeover.
remediation:
- Enable Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA) and require HTTPS on AD CS enrollment endpoints.
- Enforce SMB signing and LDAP signing/channel binding across the domain.
- Disable NTLM where possible and restrict it via policy.
- Apply patches addressing EFSRPC/coercion vectors and monitor for anomalous machine authentication.
